leading_positions.synthesis: Four members explicitly prefer B061 as the sole prize part, each with Katori and Ye as laureates. They share the scientific case: the magic-wavelength lattice lets many neutral atoms be interrogated at once, systematics were controlled to about 10^-18, and independent laboratories have compared clocks. They also share the reservation that the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 Wineland-Haroche prize cover neighbouring ground, and that Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Hinkley, Takamoto and others did essential work. They differ in emphasis: Kroll wants the citation worded narrowly for the lattice clock, not for optical clocks generally, and also calls the contribution an engineering-physics achievement, not a new phenomenon. Johansson moved to B061 from circuit QED (B018) and flags that the SI redefinition is still pending. Kroll argues a metrology decision should not drive a physics prize, while Lindroth treats the redefinition as a consequence, not a motivation. Pearce holds no strong view between B061 and B013. The four citations are similar but not identical in wording.

Four members explicitly prefer B013 as the sole prize part, with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer as laureates. They share the theory-then-experiment argument: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted flat bands at a magic angle, the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states confirmed it, and many groups have reproduced and extended it in graphene multilayers and TMD moire systems. All four name the same reservations: the field is under a decade old, the origin of the superconductivity is unsettled, and Yuan Cao (first author of the 2018 papers) and earlier band-structure work (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell and colleagues) sit outside the credited names. They differ in how binding these are. Danielsson and Mehlig name B061 as a safer fallback if maturity is decisive, and Eriksson also lists B061 as an alternative. Olsson says she wants certainty about the original credit before settling. Their second alternatives also differ: B009 for Danielsson, B019 for Eriksson, B008 for Mehlig, B061 and B019 for Olsson.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members name a single-part prize in their round-1 configuration, and only B061 and B013 appear as preferred configurations; each has four explicit supporters, so there is no majority yet.

Both leading configurations have clean-looking credited sets in the supplied names. B061 is Katori and Ye (identical pair in all four supporters). B013 is a theory-plus-experiment trio, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer (identical three names in all four supporters, though listed in a different order by Olsson).

Supporters on both sides cite independent reproduction as the decisive evidence for maturity: clock-to-clock comparisons across several countries for B061, and independent groups and spectroscopy for B013.

Members who prefer B061 name B013 as a close rival, and vice versa: B013 is an alternative for Kroll, Pearce, and B061 is an alternative for Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson. Each camp also treats the other candidate as a credible fallback.
Several members explicitly say they defer to colleagues outside their own field on the physics (Pearce on atomic and condensed-matter topics, Kroll on the condensed-matter details of B013).
No member disputes that attribution is the main open issue for B013 and that prior-prize overlap is the main open issue for B061.
scientific_disputes: Whether B061 is a distinct discovery or a third step in a precision-laser-spectroscopy tradition already honoured in 2005 (frequency comb) and 2012 (quantum control of single systems and ion clocks). Kroll calls it an engineering-physics achievement rather than a new phenomenon; Lindroth and Johansson see the many-atom magic-wavelength lattice as a genuine conceptual step beyond single-ion clocks.

Whether a precision-measurement achievement (B061) or a discovery of new quantum matter (B013) better fits the mandate. Olsson reads the mandate as favouring an experimentally verified discovery with an original experiment; Danielsson cautions that a young field's long-term importance is not yet shown.

Whether the unsettled pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene means the central physical question is still open (Eriksson, Mehlig, Danielsson, Olsson all raise it) or whether the platform and its correlated phases are already established regardless of mechanism (Danielsson and Eriksson both argue the discovery does not depend on it).

B009 (IceCube) is not a preferred configuration for any member. Danielsson ranked it first at opening and keeps it as an alternative, but Pearce notes that individual source identifications lack second-detector confirmation. Members' views of its scientific standing are therefore not tested in this round.

B019 (topological insulators) appears only as an alternative (Eriksson, Olsson) and is not a preferred configuration. Eriksson ranks it conceptually clean and well confirmed, but its status relative to the 2016 prize and to the 3D topological work was not argued by a supporter.
attribution_disputes: B013: Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 experimental papers, is outside the credited names, and the three-name limit means he cannot be added without dropping a laureate. Earlier twisted-bilayer band-structure work (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell and colleagues) may carry priority for parts of the flat-band picture. All four supporters raise this, and none has verified the record beyond memory. No supporter has resolved it from the record.

B061: Katori (concept and first realisation) and Ye (carrying strontium to the 10^-18 floor) are the credited pair, but Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Hinkley, Takamoto, Bloom and the NIST, PTB and SYRTE groups contributed to the precision result, and Ye's earlier comb work was already rewarded in 2005. Kroll in particular says the citation should name the lattice clock, not the whole field of optical clocks.

B019 (as an alternative): Eriksson notes that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe realisation and are not on the credited list, and that the 3D work of Fu, Kane, Mele and Moore-Balents and Hasan cannot fit within three names. Olsson also asks whether the credit chain can be narrowed fairly.
B009 (as an alternative): Pearce notes that AMANDA, Baikal and the IceCube founding group share credit beyond Halzen and Spiering.
maturity_disputes: B013: the experiments are under a decade old, sample-to-sample variation is large, and the superconducting mechanism is unresolved. Eriksson and Mehlig call the field young; Mehlig explicitly says that if the pairing mechanism must be understood first, B013 is early and B061 or B008 are safer. Supporters of B013 argue that reproduction across many groups and material families shows the discovery stands independently of the mechanism.

B061: the accuracy record and the clock-to-clock comparisons are mature, but the SI redefinition of the second has not happened. Kroll says the redefinition should not drive a physics prize; Lindroth and Mehlig ask how much it should count for or against timing. Mehlig asks whether members who ranked B061 first would prefer it on maturity grounds.

Whether a second condensed-matter prize soon after the 2016 topological-phases prize, and an AMO-adjacent prize soon after the 2025 superconducting-circuit award, should affect which of B013 and B061 is preferred this year (Eriksson raises the first point; Johansson cites proximity to the 2025 award as one reason he dropped B018).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology) says he should recuse himself from any B018 (circuit QED) discussion and would not vote for it as a preferred part; B018 is one of his alternatives to B061.

Kroll (rare-earth-doped crystal quantum memories) would recuse himself from any B002 deliberation concerning the rare-earth memory credit; B002 is on the shortlist but is not a preferred configuration of any member.

Pearce (chair) discloses membership in the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations, a mild proximity to B009 through Fermi-LAT follow-up of IceCube alerts, and a cosmic-ray antimatter background adjacent to B005; no direct connection to any credited person, and neither B009 nor B005 is a preferred configuration.

Mehlig notes that Johansson and Olsson share the Chalmers environment (Gothenburg) and that GU and Chalmers are closely linked, with no stated collaboration; Olsson likewise notes Johansson is at Chalmers and that she has worked with Tohoku and Tokyo microscopy communities, with no known tie to Katori.

Lindroth discloses collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and the Lund and ETH attosecond groups, which she says does not concern any shortlisted candidate; she would flag it if attosecond work reached the shortlist.
Danielsson (Princeton and Uppsala ties) and Eriksson state that no conflict is apparent for the candidates they discuss.
questions_for_round2: For B013 supporters: can the committee confirm from the historical record whether the decisive experimental credit for the 2018 observations lies with Jarillo-Herrero alone, or whether excluding Yuan Cao and contemporaneous groups makes a three-name citation unacceptable? Is the priority of earlier band-structure work (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell) strong enough to change the theory credit?

For B013 supporters: is an unresolved pairing mechanism a reason to wait, or is the establishment of correlated insulating and superconducting states in a tunable moire platform sufficient on its own for a prize this year? Please state what evidence would settle it.

For B061 supporters: what is the precise argument that a lattice-clock prize is a distinct discovery and not a third award in the 2005 and 2012 line? Kroll, please say whether the narrow wording you propose (invention and realisation of the lattice clock) fully answers the objection.

For B061 supporters: are Katori and Ye the right two names given Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Hinkley, Takamoto and Bloom, and can the citation be worded so that the 10^-18 demonstration is credited without implying the rest of the field is?

For both camps: does the SI redefinition of the second, still pending, count for, against, or not at all in the timing of B061? Kroll holds that it should not count; Mehlig and Lindroth ask the question explicitly.

For all members: given a 4-4 explicit split between B061 and B013, would each member state whether they could accept the other candidate as the 2026 prize, and on what single condition (for example, a fixed attribution or a stated maturity threshold)?

For members listing B019, B009, B034, B008 or B018 as alternatives: is any of these a preferred configuration for round 2, and if so, which attribution or maturity objection must be answered first, given that none currently has an explicit supporter?

Does the committee want to consider a multi-part configuration in round 2, given Johansson and Mehlig both raise combined prizes (B034 with B061, B008 with another achievement) and the three-person limit makes some combinations impossible without dropping a name?
summary.chair_observation: On the eight round-1 files, the committee is split four to four between B061 (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce) and B013 (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson), and no other ballot has an explicit preferred-configuration supporter. The two groups state their reservations in similar terms, as prior-prize overlap and credit boundary for B061 and maturity and attribution for B013, and several members describe the other candidate as an acceptable fallback. Round 2 should aim to settle the factual attribution questions for B013 and the novelty question for B061, not to re-argue merit already stated.
